actions.query: mechanisms of autonomous goal formation and curiosity-driven information gain in unsupervised reinforcement learning
actions.reason: Expanding the theoretical basis for autonomous problem selection as mandated by project next_step.

review.alternative: Goals may be strictly hard-coded via evolution rather than learned via hierarchy.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence showing that hierarchical decomposition fails to produce goal-directed behavior in novel environments.

claims.statement: Hierarchical planning allows agents to decompose complex objectives, facilitating autonomous problem selection.

support.explanation: This demonstrates that hierarchical decomposition is a viable pathway for agents to infer and structure goals in the absence of explicit, simple objectives.
support.passage: BIHRL is able to signiﬁcantly outperform BIRL even when we only have a weak prior on the hierarchical structure of the plans available to the agent

review.alternative: Exploration might be driven by simple noise or undirected movement rather than value-based optimism.
review.would_change_mind: Evidence that ensemble-based bonuses do not lead to meaningful discovery of new problem states.

claims.statement: Ensemble-based value estimation enables first-visit optimism, providing a mechanism for autonomous deep exploration.

support.explanation: Optimistic exploration allows agents to autonomously seek out information about uncertain transitions, a prerequisite for self-driven inquiry.
support.passage: this allows for desirable features like first-visit optimism. We show our framework allows for Optimistic Initial Values with high probability.

actions.findings:
Hierarchical planning allows agents to decompose complex objectives, facilitating autonomous problem selection. [source-80d47fc1443b41fd]

Ensemble-based value estimation enables first-visit optimism, providing a mechanism for autonomous deep exploration. [source-b2436fb7e9d04544]
actions.limitations: Existing models primarily adapt pre-defined environments; true open-ended objective discovery remains a high-level hypothesis requiring further experimental validation.
actions.next_questions: How can an intelligence distinguish between instrumental goals necessary for survival and novel, curiosity-driven problem selection?
actions.reason: Updating the notebook to incorporate hierarchical planning and instrumental succession perspectives on agency.
actions.summary: This revision integrates hierarchy-aware planning (BIHRL) and ensemble-based optimistic value estimation (VBE) to explain how agents might autonomously structure problem-solving strategies. It posits that goal specification arises not merely from external assignment but from the recursive application of preference inference, influenced by instrumental succession.
actions.title: Foundations of Autonomous Problem Formulation

proposal.summary: Advancing the investigation into autonomous problem selection by integrating hierarchical planning frameworks and optimistic value exploration, while accounting for the effects of instrumental succession on agency.
proposal.title: Institutional Journal: Synthesis of Autonomous Problem Formulation
